episodes.title: What Is Myth?
episodes.description: Explore how foundational stories express cultural identities and shape the societies that tell them.

episodes.title: Creation from the Void
episodes.description: Compare accounts in which divine action creates a universe from nothing.

episodes.title: Cosmic Sexy Time, Eggs, Seeds, and Water
episodes.description: Explore creation stories that connect cosmic beginnings with reproduction across several cultural traditions.

episodes.title: Earth Mothers and Rebellious Sons – Creation, Part 3
episodes.description: Compare Earth Mother traditions, divine family conflicts, and stories about creating humanity.

episodes.title: Social Orders and Creation Stories
episodes.description: Investigate how creation narratives can justify social hierarchies by blaming women for human suffering.

episodes.title: Humans and Nature and Creation
episodes.description: Examine the relationships between people, other organisms, and nature expressed in creation traditions.

episodes.title: Pantheons of the Ancient Mediterranean
episodes.description: Compare Sumerian and Egyptian divine families and what they suggest about their cultures.

episodes.title: Indian Pantheons
episodes.description: Explore Sanskrit traditions through Brahman, major deities, and stories of Durga.

episodes.title: The Greeks and Romans – Pantheons, Part 3
episodes.description: Compare Greek and Roman gods through their origins, family relationships, and areas of influence.

episodes.title: The Norse Pantheon
episodes.description: Meet major Norse gods and other beings within their connected mythological world.

episodes.title: African Pantheons and the Orishas
episodes.description: Explore Yoruba traditions and the Orishas of West African stories.

episodes.title: Theories of Myth
episodes.description: Compare historical scholarly approaches to studying and interpreting myths.

episodes.title: Great Goddesses
episodes.description: Explore patterns among female deities associated with fertility, fate, life, death, and regeneration.

episodes.title: Fire and Buffalo Goddesses
episodes.description: Compare stories of Pele and White Buffalo Calf Woman and consider their cultural meanings.

episodes.title: Archetypes and Male Divinities
episodes.description: Examine recurring roles of male divinities, including rulers, fathers, tricksters, and destroyers.

episodes.title: Floods in the Ancient Near East
episodes.description: Compare deluge narratives from biblical, Mesopotamian, Zoroastrian, and Roman traditions.

episodes.title: Yu the Engineer and Flood Stories from China
episodes.description: Explore Yu's flood-control achievements and his place as a model leader in Chinese tradition.

episodes.title: American Floods
episodes.description: Compare Mayan and Aztec flood narratives and their similarities across different cultural settings.

episodes.title: The Dying God
episodes.description: Investigate deities associated with dying and returning to life across several traditions.

episodes.title: Tricksters: An Introduction
episodes.description: Introduce the contradictory character of tricksters through Anansi and other examples.

episodes.title: Hermes and Loki and Tricksters, Part 2
episodes.description: Explore Hermes and Loki as creative figures whose tricks help shape their mythological cultures.

episodes.title: Coyote and Raven, American Tricksters
episodes.description: Examine Coyote and Raven stories and the creative roles of American trickster figures.

episodes.title: The Apocalyspe
episodes.description: Compare visions of judgment and the world's ending in several religious traditions.

episodes.title: Ragnarok
episodes.description: Explore the Norse apocalypse and questions about Christian influence on its written accounts.

episodes.title: The Hero’s Journey and the Monomyth
episodes.description: Investigate Campbell's proposed shared pattern of heroic storytelling and its later influence.

episodes.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh
episodes.description: Follow Gilgamesh's adventures and search for immortality through the framework of heroic journeys.

episodes.title: Rama and the Ramayana
episodes.description: Explore Rama's cultural importance and question how his story fits the hero's-journey model.

episodes.title: Galahad, Perceval, and the Holy Grail
episodes.description: Compare versions of the Grail quest centered on Perceval and Galahad.

episodes.title: The Mwindo Epic
episodes.description: Follow Mwindo's transformation from a remarkable infant into a wise leader.

episodes.title: Herakles. Or Hercules. A Problematic Hero
episodes.description: Examine Herakles's labors and life alongside the troubling features of his character.

episodes.title: Ma’ui, Oceania’s Hero
episodes.description: Explore Ma'ui as adventurer, trickster, and culture hero across Pacific Island traditions.

episodes.title: Mythical Caves and Gardens
episodes.description: Compare gardens and caves connected with the creation of worlds and human origins.

episodes.title: Mythical Mountains
episodes.description: Explore mountain stories from China and Japan and the meanings attached to imposing landscapes.

episodes.title: Mythical Trees
episodes.description: Compare significant trees in biblical, Norse, Hindu, and Buddhist traditions.

episodes.title: Cities of Myth
episodes.description: Investigate legendary origins of real cities alongside imagined urban places.

episodes.title: Monsters. They’re Us, Man
episodes.description: Explore what distinguishes monsters from other magical beings through examples including the Wendigo.

episodes.title: Mythical Horses
episodes.description: Compare extraordinary horses in stories from cultures around the world.

episodes.title: Serpents and Dragons
episodes.description: Explore dragons and serpents as sources of destruction, royal power, and life-giving rain.

episodes.title: Witches and Hags
episodes.description: Investigate stories about dangerous magical women and the social assumptions behind them.

episodes.title: Freud, Jung, Luke Skywalker, and the Psychology of Myth
episodes.description: Examine myth's influence on Freud and Jung through archetypes, unconscious thought, and modern storytelling.

episodes.title: Mythical Language and Idiom
episodes.description: Trace familiar English expressions and themes back to mythological narratives.
